papers.title: Scaffold-Constrained Generative Design Overcomes Failure Modes in Computational Protein Engineering.
papers.abstract: Applying unconstrained generative protein models to fixed structural scaffolds can produce systematic design artifacts, including glycine enrichment, grammar violations, and discordant complex predictions. We developed DARPinMPNN, a scaffold-constrained computational framework that restricts production sequence generation to permitted DARPin Greek Grammar residue pools. A state-aware chimeric multiple sequence alignment strategy supported AlphaFold2-Multimer (AF2) screening, followed by complementary AlphaFold 3 (AF3) evaluation. Of 15,000 generated variants targeting mesothelin, VEGF-A, and H
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors show that unconstrained generative protein models applied to fixed structural scaffolds produce systematic artifacts like glycine enrichment and grammar violations. They develop DARPinMPNN, a scaffold-constrained framework that restricts sequence generation to permitted DARPin Greek Grammar residue pools, and use it with AlphaFold2-Multimer and AlphaFold3 screening to design 15,000 variants targeting mesothelin, VEGF-A, and other proteins.

papers.title: What deep learning can and cannot (yet) do for enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced structure-based enzyme design, yet reliably creating highly efficient enzymes remains out of reach. One emerging enzyme design strategy combines diffusion-based scaffold generation around active-site models with sequence design. Such structure-based approaches have expanded the accessible reaction space and enabled the emergence of enzymes with diverse catalytic functions and complex catalytic motifs. Despite notable catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM), turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, suggesting that current approaches typically yield tight sub
papers.summary: This review assesses the current capabilities and limitations of deep learning for enzyme design, highlighting that while diffusion-based scaffold generation combined with sequence design has expanded accessible reaction space and produced enzymes with diverse catalytic functions, reliably achieving high efficiency remains elusive. Notably, while catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM) can be good, turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, indicating that current methods typically yield tight substrate binding but suboptimal catalysis.

papers.title: Microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase degrades metformin to limit therapeutic response in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Metformin is a first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, yet therapeutic responses vary widely. Whether gut microbes directly inactivate metformin and limit its efficacy remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase, AdhE, from Eubacterium species enriched in individuals with a low response to metformin. AdhE converts metformin to pharmacologically inactive products, lowering intestinal and systemic drug exposure. Genetic deletion of AdhE or phage-mediated depletion of AdhE-producing Eubacterium hallii MD1 restores metformin exposure and glycemic control in mi
papers.summary: This study identifies a gut microbial enzyme, aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase (AdhE), from Eubacterium species that converts metformin into inactive products, reducing drug exposure and limiting its therapeutic efficacy in type 2 diabetes. Deleting AdhE or depleting AdhE-producing E. hallii MD1 via phage restores metformin levels and improves glycemic control in mice. The findings reveal a direct microbial mechanism of drug inactivation that could explain variable metformin responses.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions at genome-wide scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate the three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method aims to overcome the limitations of 1D and 2D representation-based models, which cannot capture geometric binding-site information critical for accurate CPI prediction in early drug discovery.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors introduce MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to predict enzyme turnover numbers (kcat) by jointly modeling enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints. They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrate its utility for rational enzyme evolution. This addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalysis where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput and existing computational methods poorly capture enzyme-reaction interplay.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that GPCRs function as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes rather than isolated monomers, challenging the classical drug discovery paradigm. It synthesizes evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology to show that these complexes are relevant in brain regions tied to neuropsychiatric disease. The authors suggest targeting GPCR heteromers could improve efficacy and reduce side effects for treatment-resistant patients.

papers.title: Systematic trends in water properties across Jacob's ladder density functionals.
papers.abstract: Kohn-Sham density functional theory is the workhorse of computational materials science and chemistry, but the optimal choice of exchange-correlation approximation for a given system is often unclear. Traditional benchmark studies typically compare selected density functional approximations (DFAs) against high-level quantum chemistry results for small structures and static energies, rather than against experimental thermodynamic or response properties. Here, we show how machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) allow for molecular dynamics simulations of these properties at scale, thereb
papers.summary: This paper uses machine learning interatomic potentials to run large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of water, systematically comparing density functional approximations across Jacob's ladder against experimental thermodynamic and response properties. It reveals systematic trends in how functional choice affects predicted water behavior, offering guidance for selecting exchange-correlation approximations.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the GABPA transcription factor in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any known classification. The tumors show distinct histopathology, including loss of GLUT1 expression and a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular layer, distinguishing them from infantile hemangioma. The findings suggest GABPA dysfunction may drive a previously unrecognized vascular tumor entity.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening followed by in vitro testing to identify HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups, aiming to overcome the poor selectivity and pharmacokinetics of traditional hydroxamate inhibitors. The authors prioritized compounds forming HDAC3-specific interactions and bidentate or monodentate zinc coordination. The work provides a criteria-guided strategy for developing more selective epigenetic inhibitors.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, forms seed-competent fibrils that propagate between cells in tauopathies. The authors identify a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot that drives in-register stacking of tau molecules onto fibril templates, preventing mismatched stacking. This mechanism may explain the templated, prion-like aggregation underlying tau pathology.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a de novo protein design framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to engineer a thermostable diagnostic antigen derived from yellow fever virus NS1. By mapping the evolutionary dynamics of the YFV polyprotein, they identified conserved but discriminating regions to reduce cross-reactivity with related flaviviruses. This approach aims to improve serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review examines metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), a class of hybrid materials, as a strategy for delivering drugs across the blood-brain barrier to treat brain disorders like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke. It synthesizes mechanism-driven design principles for MPNs, from precision assembly to multidimensional synergistic therapy, addressing the complex pathophysiological microenvironment of brain diseases.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: The authors developed a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase produces linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) by using active site properties as features rather than sequence alone. This data-driven approach helps overcome the difficulty of engineering these enzymes by linking structural pockets to product specificity.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, causing large micelles to break into smaller, highly dispersed micro-aggregates. The findings suggest these enzyme-biosurfactant composites could improve interfacial activity for petroleum engineering applications.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This paper introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation. The model combines molecular graph representations with a convolutional protein sequence encoder and was benchmarked on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ against a matched GIN baseline. The study tests whether this architectural swap improves affinity prediction for applications like virtual screening and lead optimization.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates current practices in molecular docking of natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches and proposes practical guidelines to improve rigor and reproducibility in the field.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The work leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose preapproved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines protein language model sequence embeddings with predicted 3D structural features to identify effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria. By integrating geometric structural information with sequence semantics, it aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only and structure-only predictors, improving effector discovery for understanding bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods (CLEAN, ProteInter) and global structural alignment tools, which suffer from high false positive rates when proteins are globally similar but functionally distinct.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G2
papers.summary: This study combines cryo-EM and solid-state NMR to determine the atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from E. coli in lipid nanodiscs and liposomes. The cryo-EM structures capture a closed conformation of both wild-type and a low-threshold G22S mutant, while NMR provides complementary information on channel dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The work advances understanding of the structural basis of mechanosensitive channel gating.

papers.title: Microtubule destabilization by SB225002 through preferential weakening of lateral tubulin interactions revealed by structural and computational analyses.
papers.abstract: Microtubules are essential for cell division and intracellular signaling, making them well-established targets for anticancer therapy. However, the clinical utility of conventional microtubule-targeting agents is often limited by toxicity and drug resistance. SB225002, originally identified as an interleukin-8 receptor antagonist, has been reported to disrupt microtubule dynamics and exhibit anticancer activity with relatively low toxicity in preclinical studies. Yet, the structural basis of its interaction with tubulin remains poorly understood. Here, we determined the crystal structure of th
papers.summary: This study solves the crystal structure of the anticancer compound SB225002 bound to tubulin, revealing that it destabilizes microtubules by preferentially weakening lateral interactions between tubulin subunits rather than longitudinal ones. Combined structural and computational analyses clarify a novel binding mode for a drug originally developed as an interleukin-8 receptor antagonist, offering a structural rationale for its low-toxicity microtubule-disrupting activity.

papers.title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter.
papers.abstract: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavio
papers.summary: This review discusses how fluorination—the incorporation of fluorine atoms into molecules and nanoscale systems—can be used to tune their interactions with biological matter. It highlights how fluorine's unique properties (small size, high electronegativity, strong C-F bonds) improve metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and enhance pharmacokinetics, while also emerging as a tool to control molecular assembly and biological behavior in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used GNPS molecular networking combined with network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify bioactive constituents in Scoparia dulcis, an edible medicinal herb used traditionally for inflammatory disorders. The integrated approach pinpointed specific metabolites and their potential anti-inflammatory mechanisms, which were then validated experimentally. The work demonstrates how computational and analytical chemistry methods can be combined to characterize the therapeutic potential of traditional medicinal plants.

papers.title: Lipid composition-driven sorting of ABHD5 between monolayer and bilayer surfaces.
papers.abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) are ubiquitous organelles that store neutral lipids and serve as central regulators of lipid homeostasis. Their structure includes a hydrophobic core of triacylglycerols and sterol esters surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer. This organization creates biophysical properties that guide selective protein recruitment. Among LD-associated proteins, α/β-hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5, also known as CGI-58) is a key regulator of lipolysis and broader lipid metabolism, yet the mechanisms guiding its distribution between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) bilayers and LD m
papers.summary: This study investigates how the lipid composition of cellular membranes directs the localization of ABHD5 (CGI-58), a key regulator of lipid breakdown, between the phospholipid monolayer of lipid droplets and the bilayer of the endoplasmic reticulum. The findings suggest that differences in lipid composition act as a sorting signal, helping explain how ABHD5 is recruited to the right membrane surface to control lipid metabolism.

papers.title: Thermal proteome profiling identifies new drug targets in Plasmodium falciparum parasites.
papers.abstract: Spreading resistance to clinically used antimalarial drugs increases the need for identification of new drug targets. Here, we screened 25 antimalarials with known and unknown mode of action to validate old and find new drug targets in P. falciparum. Combining experimental approach by proteome-wide cellular thermal shift assay and computational filtering by molecular docking, we found the drugs to bind to previously known drug targets, validated ACS10 as the target of MMV665915 and discovered new drug targets. Furthermore, we updated the experimental and analytical MS-CETSA pipeline with the i
papers.summary: The authors used a proteome-wide cellular thermal shift assay (MS-CETSA) combined with molecular docking to screen 25 antimalarial drugs against Plasmodium falciparum, validating known targets and identifying new ones, including ACS10 as the target of MMV665915. They also improved the experimental and analytical MS-CETSA pipeline, providing a resource for antimalarial drug target discovery.

papers.title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry.
papers.abstract: Protein recognition mimicry is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies. While existing MD-based computational tools can be used to explore a particular set of mutations at a time, suitable for small-scale studies, high-throughput (HTP) exploration of protein recognition for engineering purposes
papers.summary: DyME is a molecular dynamics-based engine designed to enable high-throughput exploration of protein mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry. It addresses the limitation of existing MD tools that can only handle small sets of mutations at a time, allowing larger-scale analysis of how amino acid changes affect molecular recognition.

papers.title: Computational identification of potential inhibitors for chikungunya virus nsP2pro.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus remains a crucial global health issue with no approved therapy available. In particular, the viral replication is associated with the non-structural protein 2 protease (nsP2pro). In this study, possible inhibitors for nsP2pro from the National Cancer Institute (NCI) database were screened via computational approaches. Molecular docking simulations were initially predicted top potential ligands. MD simulations were then performed to refine the ligand binding pose. During the equilibrium intervals, the ligands formed rigid contacts with the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr5
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen compounds from the NCI database for inhibitors of the chikungunya virus nsP2 protease (nsP2pro), a key enzyme in viral replication. Several top candidate ligands were identified that form stable, rigid contacts with key active-site residues such as Asn476, Ala511, and Tyr512. These computational hits provide starting points for further experimental validation as potential antiviral therapeutics.

papers.title: Semi-Rational Design of CpNampt Mutants for Enhanced Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) Synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstract: β-Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) serves as a direct precursor of the essential cofactor NAD⁺, playing a crucial role in regulating mitochondrial function and delaying cellular aging. Synthetic biology, with its environmental and economic advantages, has become an important approach for the production of natural medicines, with the optimized design of metabolic pathways at its core. In this study, we focused on the NMN‑consuming pathway mediated by the nma1 and pof1 genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and consequently generated their double‑knockout mutant, DHSX02. Futhermore, a highly efficie
papers.summary: This study engineers Saccharomyces cerevisiae for enhanced production of β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), an NAD+ precursor linked to mitochondrial function and aging. The authors knocked out the NMN-consuming genes nma1 and pof1 to create strain DHSX02, then applied semi-rational design to generate CpNampt mutants with improved NMN synthesis. The work demonstrates a synthetic biology strategy for more efficient NMN production.

papers.title: Opening the black box: study of the multi-target anticancer mechanisms of Ecballium elaterium cucurbitacins via in vitro, network pharmacology, and molecular docking analyses.
papers.abstract: Ecballium elaterium is a perennial plant species that belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family. In this study, we examined the biological activities and analyzed the chemical profiles of ethyl acetate, acetone, aqueous acetone, and water extracts from different parts (aerial parts, fruit peels, and seeds) of E. elaterium. We performed chemical characterization using UPLC-ESI-MS/MS. To investigate the biological activities of the extracts, antioxidant capacity, enzyme inhibition, and cytotoxicity assays were conducted. Thirty-eight compounds were detected in the extracts, and cucurbitacins and their
papers.summary: This study characterizes the chemical composition of Ecballium elaterium extracts from different plant parts using UPLC-ESI-MS/MS, identifying 38 compounds including cucurbitacins. Through in vitro assays, network pharmacology, and molecular docking, the authors explore the multi-target anticancer mechanisms of these cucurbitacins, revealing potential interactions with multiple cancer-related targets.

papers.title: Lipid gating of BK channels and activation mechanism by negatively charged lipids.
papers.abstract: BK channels are a class of K+ channels that possess an unusually high conductance and are synergistically gated by intracellular Ca2+ and voltage. Despite the significant array of experimental and computational data, many aspects of their function and dynamics remain unclear - such as how ion permeation is halted in the closed state of the channel. Available CryoEM structures obtained in deactivating conditions capture the channel with a wide, unobstructed pore, in contrast to e.g., a helix bundle crossing observed in some K+ channels. Several hypotheses of BK closure were proposed, including
papers.summary: This study uses computational modeling to investigate how negatively charged lipids regulate BK potassium channel gating and how the channel closes despite cryo-EM structures showing an apparently open pore. The work proposes a lipid-dependent mechanism for channel closure, addressing a long-standing puzzle in BK channel biophysics.

papers.title: Advances in the projected forces and momenta decoherence method for attosecond nonadiabatic molecular dynamics.
papers.abstract: The Projected Forces and Momenta (PFM) decoherence correction has recently been introduced [J. Chem. Theory Comput., 2025, 21, 10645] and successfully applied for trajectory surface-hopping (TSH) simulations describing the coupled electron-nuclear dynamics originating from coherent superpositions of molecular electronic states generated by broadband laser excitation. In this work, we extend the capabilities of TSH-PFM for the simulation of a broader range of nonadiabatic dynamics. First, we showcase the inclusion of the explicit interaction with a broadband pulse and apply it to the LiH molecu
papers.summary: This paper extends the Projected Forces and Momenta (PFM) decoherence correction method for trajectory surface-hopping simulations of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics. The authors add explicit treatment of broadband laser pulse interactions and demonstrate the approach on the LiH molecule, broadening the applicability of TSH-PFM to a wider range of photoinduced dynamics.

papers.title: Evaluation of 6-substituted coumarins as SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors: enzymatic, cellular, and computational insights.
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) plays a crucial role in viral replication, making it an attractive target for antiviral drug development. This study evaluates the inhibitory potential of nineteen 6-substituted coumarin derivatives (1a-p and 2a-c) against Mpro using a FRET-based enzymatic assay. Among them, the chlorinated derivative 1f (AKE-9306) exhibited the highest potency with an IC50 value of 61.77 µM. Enzyme kinetics analysis through Michaelis-Menten and Lineweaver-Burk plots revealed that compound 1f may act through a mixed-type inhibition mechanism with a preference for the free en
papers.summary: This study screened nineteen 6-substituted coumarin derivatives for their ability to inhibit the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro), a key enzyme for viral replication. The chlorinated derivative 1f (AKE-9306) was the most potent, with an IC50 of 61.77 µM, and kinetic analysis suggested a mixed-type inhibition mechanism. The work combines enzymatic, cellular, and computational approaches to characterize these potential antiviral compounds.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a sequence-based method for predicting antibody paratope residues that incorporates antigen context, unlike prior sequence-based predictors that are largely antigen-agnostic. It uses an Expectation-Maximization framework to make antigen-aware predictions without requiring antibody structural inputs, addressing a key limitation of structure-based approaches that need experimentally determined complexes.

papers.title: DesignMaster: a multi-conditional diffusion framework for rational PROTAC design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTAC molecules, which are bifunctional compounds that degrade target proteins via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. The method incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control, addressing limitations of prior structure-based and fragment-based approaches. This enables more controllable and drug-like PROTAC generation.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study evaluates the anti-inflammatory properties of Cotula cinerea essential oil using a combination of chemical profiling (GC-MS), in vivo rat experiments, histological analysis, and computational modeling. The oil's main components—trans-thujone, santolina triene, and sabinene—were associated with reduced liver and kidney indices and improved blood parameters in treated rats, suggesting potential anti-inflammatory benefits.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is a promising anticancer target, and the marine natural product space remains underexplored for this purpose. The integrated computational approach aims to prioritize candidate inhibitors for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Thiolactomycin-based morpholino and piperidino conjugates: synthesis, antimalarial evaluation, and PfFAS-II inhibition.
papers.abstract: Malaria remains a formidable global healthcare challenge due to emerging drug-resistant Plasmodium spp., underscoring the urgent need for novel antimalarial scaffolds. Thiolactomycin, a FAS-II inhibitor, is a promising lead for structural optimization. This study aims to design, synthesize, and evaluate a series of thiomorpholino and piperidino conjugates bearing a thiolactone moiety as target-specific antimalarial agents.
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of new thiolactomycin-inspired compounds, where the natural thiolactone scaffold is conjugated to morpholine or piperidine groups, and evaluates them as antimalarial agents targeting the Plasmodium falciparum FAS-II enzyme. The conjugates were tested for antimalarial activity and PfFAS-II inhibition, aiming to overcome drug-resistant Plasmodium strains.

papers.title: Synthesis, in vitro and in silico evaluation of quinazoline and triazoloquinazoline derivatives as PDE7A inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Phosphodiesterase 7A (PDE7A) is an attractive therapeutic target for the treatment of inflammatory, autoimmune, and neurodegenerative disorders through modulation of intracellular cAMP levels. However, the development of highly potent and selective PDE7A inhibitors remains challenging. This study aimed to design, synthesize, and evaluate 2-chloroquinazoline and fused 1,2,4-triazolo[4,3-c]quinazoline derivatives as potential PDE7A inhibitors, supported by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in silico toxicity prediction.
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of 2-chloroquinazoline and fused triazoloquinazoline derivatives as potential inhibitors of the phosphodiesterase enzyme PDE7A, a target for inflammatory, autoimmune, and neurodegenerative diseases. The compounds were evaluated using in vitro assays alongside computational approaches including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in silico toxicity prediction to assess their inhibitory potential and drug-likeness.

papers.title: Origin-specific metabolomic profiling and network pharmacology propose potential multi-target antioxidant mechanisms of black sesame seeds.
papers.abstract: Black Sesame Seeds (BSS) are consumed as an edible herbal food with medicinal food homology and possess potent antioxidant properties; however, their metabolic compositions and corresponding antioxidant efficacies substantially vary across different geographical origins. This study investigates the underlying multi-component and multi-target antioxidant mechanisms of BSS from various geographical origins. An integrated computational and experimental approach combining UHPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS/MS-based metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking was employed. Metabolomic profi
papers.summary: This study combined UHPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS/MS metabolomics with network pharmacology and molecular docking to profile black sesame seeds from different geographical origins. The authors identified origin-specific metabolite differences and proposed multi-component, multi-target antioxidant mechanisms underlying these variations. The work links chemical composition to antioxidant efficacy through an integrated computational-experimental framework.

papers.title: Trypsinogen Pro-Region as a Molecular Scaffold for the Design of Competitive Peptide Inhibitors of Trypsin-Like Proteases.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) productivity is severely impacted by the velvetbean caterpillar Anticarsia gemmatalis Hübner, 1818 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae), a major defoliating pest in soybean-producing regions. Current management strategies rely heavily on chemical insecticides, which are associated with environmental risks and the development of resistance. Protease inhibitors have emerged as a promising alternative, as protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae is primarily mediated by trypsin-like serine proteases. In this context, the rational design of short inhibitory peptides represents
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: This paper explores using the pro-region of trypsinogen as a molecular scaffold to rationally design short competitive peptide inhibitors targeting trypsin-like serine proteases in lepidopteran pests such as Anticarsia gemmatalis. The approach aims to provide an environmentally friendly alternative to chemical insecticides by disrupting protein digestion in soybean pests. The abstract is truncated, so full experimental validation and inhibitor efficacy are not detailed.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cell populations in both the decidua (uterine lining) and peripheral blood across early and late pregnancy. It reveals dynamic changes in NK cell phenotypes and molecular states that likely support fetal tolerance and immune adaptation during gestation. The findings provide a detailed immune atlas of pregnancy-relevant NK cells.

papers.title: Evolutionary and structural pathways of antibody maturation reveal principles for engineering potent SARS-CoV-2 neutralizers.
papers.abstract: The continual emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants underscores the need to elucidate antibody maturation and apply rational design principles to optimize therapeutics. This study focused on vaccine-elicited 9C lineage, encoded by IGHV4-34, as a model for affinity maturation and structural refinement. Sequence analyses revealed strong framework conservation alongside focused diversification within CDRH3, where the invariant RWFD anchor and a recurrent SYTV block were consistently associated with potent neutralization. Phylogenetic reconstruction traced a trajectory from weakly neutralizing precurso
papers.summary: This study traces the evolutionary and structural maturation of a vaccine-elicited antibody lineage (9C, IGHV4-34) against SARS-CoV-2, showing that framework regions stay conserved while diversification concentrates in CDRH3. Specific sequence motifs—an invariant RWFD anchor and a recurrent SYTV block—are linked to potent neutralization, and phylogenetic reconstruction maps the path from weak precursors to strong neutralizers. These principles could guide rational engineering of more potent SARS-CoV-2 antibody therapeutics.

papers.title: Effects of lawsone and lawsone methyl ether on cyclooxygenase activity, redox balance, and organ-specific toxicity: An integrated computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Redox imbalance contributes significantly to the initiation and progression of inflammatory responses. Although conventional anti-inflammatory drugs are widely used, their prolonged administration is associated with a number of adverse effects. Lawsone methyl ether (LME) and lawsone are plant-derived, redox-active naphthoquinones, exhibiting diverse pharmacological activities; however, their cyclooxygenase (COX)-inhibitory effects, redox-modulatory properties, and oral toxicity profiles remain insufficiently characterized. Therefore, this study investigated the COX-inhibitory activity, redox-m
papers.summary: This study investigates two plant-derived naphthoquinones, lawsone and lawsone methyl ether, for their ability to inhibit cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes, modulate redox balance, and cause organ-specific toxicity. Using combined computational and experimental approaches, the authors characterize these compounds as potential anti-inflammatory agents while assessing their safety profiles. The work highlights both the therapeutic potential and toxicological concerns of these redox-active natural products.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds GSTP1 and enhances its catalytic activity, as shown by biophysical binding assays and enzyme kinetics. Since GSTP1 is often silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma, chemically boosting residual enzyme activity could offer a new therapeutic angle for prostate cancer.

papers.title: Immunoinformatics-based design of a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate targeting the major human-infecting hepatitis E virus genotypes 1-4.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is one of the leading causes of acute and chronic hepatitis among humans across the globe and is linked to severe diseases in immunocompromised individuals and pregnant women. Despite its substantial global burden, only one vaccine is licensed (in China and Pakistan), limiting its global accessibility. Furthermore, no globally approved mRNA vaccine against HEV is currently available, highlighting the need to develop strategies for alternative vaccines.
papers.summary: This study uses immunoinformatics to design a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate targeting the four major human-infecting hepatitis E virus genotypes (1-4). The authors computationally identified and combined B-cell and T-cell epitopes to create a construct intended to provide broad genotype coverage, addressing the lack of a globally approved HEV mRNA vaccine. The work is a computational design study, so experimental validation of immunogenicity and protective efficacy remains to be performed.

papers.title: Computational identification of natural CXCR4-binding candidates relevant to endometriosis and ovarian cancer progression.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis and ovarian cancer share invasive, inflammatory, and pro-survival mechanisms in which CXCR4 signaling may play an important role, yet phytochemical modulators of this receptor remain insufficiently characterized. This study addressed that gap by integrating receptor reconstruction, ligand-guided docking, pharmacokinetic and toxicity prediction, pharmacophore mapping, density functional theory, replicated membrane-embedded molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA analysis. A native human CXCR4 model was generated using SWISS-MODEL with 98.2% template coverage and 100% sequence identity, wh
papers.summary: This study computationally screened natural phytochemicals for their ability to bind CXCR4, a receptor implicated in both endometriosis and ovarian cancer progression. Using docking, pharmacokinetic/toxicity prediction, pharmacophore mapping, DFT, and membrane-embedded molecular dynamics with MM/GBSA, the authors identified candidate natural compounds with favorable binding and drug-like properties. The work provides a computational pipeline and candidate list for further experimental validation of CXCR4-targeting natural products.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation methods to screen phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins linked to lung cancer. The authors identify candidate compounds that may bind key oncogenic targets in non-small cell lung cancer, suggesting these natural products warrant further experimental testing. The work is entirely in silico, so findings are preliminary and require wet-lab validation.

papers.title: A computational-first proof-of-concept for dual-function metal chelation and aggregate neutralization in an Aβ42 Drosophila model.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology is amplified by a self-reinforcing metal-Aβ-ROS axis, in which redox-active Cu and Fe bound to Aβ N-terminal histidines catalyze Fenton-like ROS generation and accelerate aggregation. Existing single-target interventions - anti-amyloid antibodies, antioxidants, metal-protein attenuating compounds, aggregation inhibitors, and photooxygenation catalysts - each address only one node of this loop. We used a computational-first framework to evaluate a dual-function strategy targeting two connected points of the axis: upstream redox-active metal sequestration by ma
papers.summary: This study uses a computational-first approach to design a dual-function molecule that both chelates redox-active metals (Cu, Fe) and neutralizes Aβ42 aggregates in a Drosophila model of Alzheimer's disease. The strategy targets two connected nodes of the metal-Aβ-ROS axis, aiming to break the self-reinforcing cycle that drives AD pathology. The proof-of-concept demonstrates feasibility of simultaneously addressing metal sequestration and aggregation in vivo.

papers.title: Systems-level analysis uncovers eight hub genes and a resveratrol-based therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The pathology involves complex interactions between vascular injury, immune dysregulation, metabolic imbalance, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Traditional single-gene or single-dataset approaches have limitations in capturing the multifactorial nature of the disease. We developed a comprehensive systems-level bioinformatics framework integrating five publicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE119121, GSE146882, GSE22255, GSE37587, GSE58
papers.summary: This study integrates five public transcriptomic datasets from ischemic stroke patients to identify eight hub genes and proposes resveratrol as a potential therapeutic strategy. The systems-level framework combines multiple datasets to capture the multifactorial nature of stroke pathology, linking vascular injury, immune dysregulation, metabolic imbalance, and mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for Parkinson's disease: from transcriptome to drug interaction.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with limited therapeutic options. Acupuncture may serve as a complementary intervention, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify PD-associated diagnostic candidate genes and explore their relationship with acupuncture-related temporal expression patterns.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate diagnostic genes for Parkinson's disease and links them to acupuncture-related temporal expression patterns and potential drug interactions. It aims to uncover novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets, positioning acupuncture as a complementary intervention with molecular rationale.

papers.title: Shenling Qige Granules inhibit esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression in TE-1 xenograft and cell-based models by modulating the DCN-TGF-β/Smad signaling axis.
papers.abstract: Shenling Qige Granules (SLQG), derived from the Qing Dynasty formula Qige San recorded in Yi Xue Xin Wu, has been used in clinical practice in China as an adjuvant traditional Chinese medicine preparation for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its molecular basis remains unclear. This study investigated the antitumor effects and mechanisms of SLQG using TE-1 xenograft mice and SLQG-containing serum-treated TE-1 cells. Transcriptome sequencing, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and public-database analysis were integrated to prioritize candidate
papers.summary: This study shows that Shenling Qige Granules (SLQG), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, can inhibit esophageal squamous cell carcinoma growth in both mouse xenograft and cell-based models. Using transcriptomics, network pharmacology, and molecular simulations, the authors identify the DCN-TGF-β/Smad signaling axis as the likely mechanism of action.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a potential lead for prostate cancer treatment, developed through molecular hybridization of pharmacologically active heterocycles. The compound was evaluated preclinically using integrated mechanistic approaches to assess its anticancer activity, addressing the need for new therapies in androgen deprivation therapy-resistant disease.

papers.title: Integrated AUF-UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify COX-2-targeted constituents of Shaoyao Gancao decoction.
papers.abstract: Shaoyao Gancao Decoction (SGD), a classical multi-ingredient herbal formula, exerts potent anti-inflammatory and anti-rheumatoid arthritis effects against rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Existing cellular experiments have proven that SGD can downregulate Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression in inflammatory macrophages, implying a potential link between its anti-arthritic efficacy and COX-2 modulation. Nevertheless, its constituents with potential COX-2 binding capacity and corresponding anti-RA material basis are unclear, hindering its pharmaceutical exploitation. In this study, an integrated strate
papers.summary: This study combines analytical chemistry (AUF-UPLC-MS) with fraction-activity correlation to identify which chemical constituents of Shaoyao Gancao Decoction, a traditional Chinese herbal formula, are responsible for inhibiting COX-2, an inflammation-related enzyme. The approach links specific compounds in the decoction to anti-inflammatory activity, helping clarify the formula's anti-rheumatoid arthritis material basis.

papers.title: Mitochondria affect antibacterial immunity in cross talk with innate immune response molecules coded by genes of nuclear origin.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria are dynamic, semi-autonomous organelles that, in addition to their central role in ATP production, regulate calcium homeostasis, iron metabolism, apoptosis, and innate immune signalling. Although the mitochondrial genome encodes only 37 genes, mitochondrial architecture, bioenergetic function, and dynamics are governed predominantly by nuclear-encoded proteins, necessitating highly coordinated communication between mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and the nuclear genome. Disruption of this bidirectional mitochondrial-nuclear crosstalk has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis
papers.summary: This review examines how mitochondria, though containing their own small genome, rely heavily on nuclear-encoded proteins to regulate antibacterial innate immunity. It highlights how disrupted mitochondrial-nuclear communication contributes to immune dysfunction and disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: BDE-47 and male infertility: integrated network toxicology, single-cell transcriptomics, and in vitro evidence of GSTM1 downregulation and ferroptosis-related molecular remodeling in Leydig cells.
papers.abstract: BDE-47 is a widely detected polybrominated diphenyl ether with potential male reproductive toxicity, but the key testicular cell populations and molecular basis remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the environmental pollutant BDE-47 may impair male fertility by combining network toxicology, single-cell transcriptomics, and in vitro experiments. The authors identify Leydig cells as a key target and link BDE-47 exposure to downregulation of GSTM1 and molecular changes related to ferroptosis.

papers.title: Nanozymes in Tumor Microenvironment Modulation for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central regulatory role in malignant tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, and its complexity and dynamic heterogeneity markedly limit the efficacy of current treatment strategies. Therefore, the development of novel functional materials capable of effectively remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic tolerance has become an important research direction in cancer therapy. In recent years, nanozymes, as a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity, have shown broad potential in TME intervention and
papers.summary: This review discusses how nanozymes—nanomaterials that mimic natural enzyme catalytic activity—can be used to remodel the tumor microenvironment and overcome immunosuppression and therapeutic resistance in cancer. It highlights the potential of these functional materials as a new direction for improving cancer treatment efficacy.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, showing its expression pattern, clinical relevance, and cellular localization, and uses structure-based virtual screening to identify ethyl rosmarinate as a potential SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate. The findings suggest SLC1A6 may be a druggable target in bladder cancer, with ethyl rosmarinate as a lead compound for further development.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK) to identify FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed as antivirals. The approach highlights TMK as a promising target for mpox therapy and nominates candidate compounds for further testing.
